text: A continuous chromia-rich external layer establishes the dominant protective barrier over the alloy substrate.
evidence_basis: XRD and cross-sectional characterization show a continuous Cr2O3-dominated external scale.

text: Al undergoes internal selective oxidation as discrete alumina-rich regions preferentially distributed along subsurface grain boundaries.
evidence_basis: Elemental mapping identifies grain-boundary Al-rich internal oxide beneath the external scale.

text: Ti-containing oxide begins to occur within the external oxide assemblage while chromia remains the dominant scale constituent.
evidence_basis: Phase and elemental characterization show temperature-dependent Ti enrichment and TiO2 formation in the scale.

text: Chromium diffusion through chromia controls scale growth while grain-boundary alumina restricts coupled inward oxygen and outward chromium transport.
evidence_basis: Authors identify Cr diffusion control and grain boundaries as O and Cr transport paths.

text: The oxide scale remains substantially compact and continuous without appreciable scale exfoliation or localized structural failure.
evidence_basis: Surface observations show exfoliated oxide is hardly present and cross-sections retain an intact scale.

text: Grain-boundary alumina restricts inward oxygen and outward chromium diffusion, providing a beneficial interaction with the chromia-controlled oxidation process.
evidence_basis: Authors state that internal Al2O3 hinders oxygen ingress and outward chromium transport.
